# #2128 Generated bytecode by dxc has very higher compression ratio

**Verdict: repros.** Filed 2019-04-18 — the oldest untriaged open issue. Measured on
`main-debug` (`dxcompiler.dll: 1.10(5433-ab540090)(1.9.0.5433)`, commit `ab5400907`) against
`fxc.exe` 10.0.26100.0 from the Windows SDK.

Unusually for a size report, the claim **is** compiler-verifiable — no GPU or runtime is needed
— and the reporter's own numbers reproduce to within a few percent.

## How this was measured (a human can repeat it)

Everything is in `measure.py`, committed beside this file:

```
cd data/issues/2128
python measure.py            # dxc vs fxc, per shader and per container part
python measure.py --history  # whole-corpus ratio for every cached release
python measure.py --parts <dxc.exe> <tag>
```

Captured output: `manual-case-compression.txt`, `manual-case-history.txt`,
`manual-case-v141907-parts.txt`. Compiler paths come from `DXC` / `FXC` environment variables
with repo- and SDK-relative fallbacks; the scratch directory is created by the script.

- **Corpus (agent-constructed — the issue supplied no code).** `corpus-small.hlsl`,
  `repro.hlsl` (a realistic PBR pixel shader), `corpus-large.hlsl`. Each compiles under both
  compilers: `-T ps_6_0 -E main -O3` for dxc, `/T ps_5_1 /E main /O3` for fxc. fxc cannot emit
  SM6; that migration is exactly the comparison the reporter made.
- **Ratio = `len(raw_deflate(bytes)) / len(bytes)`**, level 9, `wbits=-15`. Raw deflate is what
  a `.zip` member uses, and a `.zip` compresses each member independently — the right model
  for "if I will zip same shaders".
- **Container split** uses the layout in `include/dxc/DxilContainer/DxilContainer.h`
  (`DxilContainerHeader` / `DxilPartHeader`). The DXIL container reuses the DXBC container
  format, so one parser handles both and the per-part numbers are directly comparable.

### Harness controls (declared in `expected.md` before anything ran)

| input | ratio | required | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 B sha256 chain | 1.001 | ≥ 0.98 | PASS |
| `repro.hlsl` source text | 0.398 | ≤ 0.50 | PASS |

Both ends of the scale are pinned, so a harness that always answers "compresses badly" (which
is indistinguishable from the reported bug) is ruled out. They re-run on every invocation.

## Result 1 — the reported ratios reproduce

`corpus-large.hlsl` is a 32× `[unroll]`, so its object is 32 near-identical blocks and is
artificially compressible for **both** compilers (fxc reaches 0.059 on it). The subset totals
excluding it are the representative figures:

| configuration | raw | zipped | ratio | reporter said |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fxc | 5516 | 1825 | **0.331** | ~0.30 |
| dxc, default | 11152 | 6833 | 0.613 | — |
| dxc `-Qstrip_reflect` | 6992 | 5389 | **0.771** | 0.80–0.85 |
| **zipped multiple, dxc ÷ fxc** | | | **3.74×** | ~3× |
| zipped multiple, both stripped | | | 4.30× | — |

Over all three shaders the multiple is 5.72× zipped, while **raw** sizes differ by only 1.5%
(46,516 vs 47,224) — dxc is larger on the two small shaders and smaller on the large one
(35,364 vs 41,708). The gap is compressibility alone, which is precisely what @Division
reported in 2022 ("size of a single uncompressed shader in dx12 is smaller").

The DXIL part measured on its own, today:

```
repro.hlsl         DXIL   3804   3224   0.848
corpus-small.hlsl  DXIL   1844   1660   0.900
```

That is the reporter's 80–85% band, unqualified.

**Why:** DXIL is LLVM 3.7 bitcode (`docs/DXIL.rst:151`), a bit-packed VBR-with-abbreviations
encoding that is already near entropy-dense, so deflate finds little to remove. DXBC's `SHEX`
chunk is byte-aligned 32-bit tokens with heavy repetition, and deflates to 0.271 on the same
shader. This is a property of the container format, not of code generation.

## Result 2 — nothing has changed in seven years

`measure.py --history`, all 20 cached releases, identical arguments:

| built | tag | bytes | deflated | ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2019-07-15 | v1.4.1907 | 78409 | 40999 | 0.523 |
| 2020-10-22 | v1.5.2010 | 47521 | 26996 | 0.568 |
| 2021-12-08 | v1.6.2112 | 46669 | 24768 | 0.531 |
| 2023-08-14 | v1.7.2308 | 46568 | 24752 | 0.532 |
| 2025-05-24 | v1.8.2505 | 46392 | 24610 | 0.530 |
| 2026-07-29 | v1.9.2607 | 46464 | 24645 | 0.530 |
| (ground truth) | main-debug | 46516 | 24609 | 0.529 |

Flat. The bisection floor is v1.4.1907 (2019-07), three months after the report, so
`always-repro'd` means "for as long as it is possible to check".

### The half of @BitMD's 2019 comment that *was* delivered

> "the DXIL size is too high and it does not compress well. We are working on this now."

Two claims; one was fixed and one never was. `manual-case-v141907-parts.txt`:

| | v1.4.1907 | v1.5.2010 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `corpus-large.hlsl` DXIL part | 68700 B | 32844 B |
| `STAT` part | *absent* | 2364 B |
| DXIL part ratio (`repro.hlsl`) | 0.839 | 0.851 |

Reflection metadata used to live inside the DXIL module; from v1.5.2010 it is stripped out and
a reduced clone is written as a separate `STAT` part (`DxilContainerAssembler.cpp:2085-2115`,
`CloneModuleForReflection` → `StripAndCreateReflectionStream`). Corpus raw size fell 39% and
zipped size 34%. **The compressibility of the bitcode did not move at all** — 0.839 → 0.851 →
0.848 today.

### A trap in the ratio itself

The whole-container ratio *improved* (0.784 → 0.636 on `repro.hlsl`) while the zipped byte
count for `corpus-small.hlsl` got **worse** (2106 B at v1.4.1907 → 2393 B today). `STAT` is a
clone of the module, so deflate deduplicates it against `DXIL` — for `corpus-small.hlsl` the
whole file deflates to 2393 B where the parts deflated individually total 3490 B. Adding
redundant data lowers the ratio without lowering the byte count. **Ratio is the wrong metric;
zipped bytes for a fixed corpus is the right one.**

## Result 3 — @Division's 2022 question, unanswered for four years

> "On xbox I used `__XBOX_DISABLE_SHADER_OBJECT_COMPRESSION` … Is there a similar parameter
> for PC dxc?"

**No, and there is nothing to disable.** zlib is reachable from exactly two places in this
repo, and neither touches the shader object:

- `lib/DxilPdbInfo/DxilPdbInfoWriter.cpp:31` — the PDB (`-Fd` / `-Zi`)
- `tools/clang/tools/dxcompiler/dxcshadersourceinfo.cpp:425` — the `SRCI` embedded-source part

`DxilContainerAssembler` writes every part uncompressed. The density @Division observed is the
LLVM bitcode encoding itself, which has no off switch — so the Xbox workaround has no PC
analogue, and asking for one is really asking for a different container encoding.

The available mitigations are `-Qstrip_reflect`, `-Qstrip_debug`, `-Qstrip_rootsignature`,
`-Qstrip_priv`, `-Qstrip_reflect_from_dxil` (`include/dxc/Support/HLSLOptions.td:537-561`).
`-Qstrip_reflect` is worth 13.5% raw and 8.7% zipped on this corpus (24609 → 22469 B) — real,
but it does not close a 3.7× gap, exactly as @BitMD said in 2019.

## Against `expected.md`

The pre-committed rule ("confirms" = dxc ratio ≥ 0.70 **and** fxc ≤ 0.45) is met by
`dxc -Qstrip_reflect` on the non-unrolled subset (0.771 / 0.318) and **not** by dxc's default
flags (0.613). That is not goalpost-moving, and the distinction is evidenced: the nearest
measurable release to the report, v1.4.1907 (three months later), emits **no `STAT` part at
all**, so the reporter's container had the shape today's `-Qstrip_reflect` produces — and
v1.4.1907 measures 0.813 / 0.784 on those same two shaders, squarely in the reported band. The
rule keyed on a denominator whose composition changed after the report; see `method-notes.md`.

## Assessment

Confirmed, unchanged since it is possible to check, and correctly deferred rather than closed.
It is not a defect — the compiler emits correct code, and raw sizes are within 1.5% of fxc's
across the corpus. It is a property of choosing LLVM bitcode as the shipping format, and the
cost lands on shipped cache size for titles with thousands of shaders. Fixing it means changing
or post-processing the container encoding, which is a product decision, not a triage one.

Three people have asked for an update since (2020, 2020, 2022) and none was given. The lowest
cost useful action is a maintainer answer on the thread — even "no change planned" — plus the
`-Qstrip_reflect` figure above and the "there is no PC equivalent" answer to @Division.
